events.title: Code to the Moon by AACI YTI

cases.refreshed: In this workshop, students create their own "Animated Rocket Launch" project in Scratch, using "broadcast" to create a countdown, ignition, and liftoff sequence that directs their rocket into space. Additionally, students will discover the science underlying actual rocket launches, beginning with a balloon demonstration of Newton's Third Law and escape velocity before learning about the Space Launch System (SLS), NASA's most powerful rocket to date. Recommended for ages 8-12. Free. Registration Required.

cases.refreshed: Experience the soothing calm of yoga and meditation, as presented by our partner, The Heartfulness Institute each Saturday. Yoga is taught by certified instructors and meditation is taught by a Heartfulness certified instructor. Yoga may be either chair or regular yoga. The program structure is 75 minutes as described below: 5 min Meet & greet 35 min Yoga and Pranayama (different styles like hatha or arkaya yoga) 5 min posture change break 25 min Heartfulness Relaxation & Meditation (experience, hands-on) This program is geared to enrich the lives of adults and seniors. Please note that all NEW participants will need to complete the Exercise Waiver in order to be able to participate. The Exercise Waiver must be completed before your first day of participation. Exercise Waivers will be provided at each meeting.

events.title: Master Gardeners: The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces

cases.refreshed: Join a Santa Clara County Master Gardener for a monthly talk on various topics. This month: Are you experiencing the "holiday guest stress syndrome"? Don't let the pressure of having a perfect tablescape wilt your holiday spirit! Join Uc Master Gardeners Laura Westley and Bernie Day for an inspiring, hands-on demonstration designed to take the stress—and the high cost—out of holiday decorating. You don't need a professional florist or a massive budget to create a "wow" factor for your dining room. What You'll Learn: The Art of the "Found" Object: Learn how to scout your own backyard or junk drawer for unique textures, greenery, and accents that add character to any arrangement. Grocery Store Glam: Discover how to deconstruct those affordable supermarket flower bunches and reimagine them into high-end-looking centerpieces. Pro-Tips for Longevity: Get the inside scoop on keeping your flora fresh from the first toast to the final slice of pie. Why join us? Whether you're hosting a grand feast or an intimate gathering, you'll walk away with the confidence and practical skills to transform "ordinary" items into extraordinary focal points. Upcoming topics are: November 14 - The Thrifty Table: Creating Beautiful Holiday Centerpieces. - no talk in December -. Detailed program descriptions to be updated when available. Free. No registration required.

events.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines as a Branch Buddy

cases.refreshed: Every now and then, libraries need a little extra love from the communities they serve. Volunteer away your fines at a rate of $20 per hour while helping the library maintain a clean and welcoming environment. Volunteers are needed to help with: Book cover cleaning - Use disinfecting wipes to reinvigorate dingy books; Children's toys cleanup - Use disinfecting wipes to disinfect children's toys; Material inspection - Check books for torn pages, pen marks, etc. Tabletop/windows/grounds cleanup - Help reinvigorate our branch by wiping down tabletops, cleaning dusty windows, and picking up litter and sweeping outside the library. Details and Requirements: Must be able to commit to the full session; Anyone under the age of 15 must volunteer alongside a parent/guardian; No experience or special skills necessary. To register, please call 408-808-3045 during library open hours or email Yannina.Yang@sjlibrary.org

events.title: Terrarium Workshop for Teens and Adults

cases.refreshed: For Teens and Adults, space limited to 30 participants. Tickets to participate will be available at the information desk 1 hour before the program starts, no sooner. Ivan the Angelfish provides people with a sense of comfort and helps de-stress others. We have provided many senior homes with terrariums or aquariums in the past and have found that it helps them relax. For our teen and adult audience, building aquariums is a fun way to engage with others and build a sense of community for your library's community. We teach people environmental science and ecology, help them build, and even let them take their terrarium/aquariums home to enjoy. Ivan the Angelfish builds environments that heal elders, teach children, and connect communities to the natural world. Free, Tickets to Participate at Info Desk at 11 AM
